definitions.explanation: A celestial body that generates its own light through nuclear fusion, as opposed to planets which reflect light. The sun is the nearest star to Earth.

examples.japanese: ⟦{太陽|たいよう}→太陽：03398_taiyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{恒星|こうせい}だ。
{恒星|こうせい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{自|みずか}ら→自ら：00287_mizukara⟧⟦{光|ひかり}→光：01707_hikari⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{放|はな}つ→放つ：10062_hanatsu⟧⟦{天体|てんたい}→天体：06361_tentai⟧⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧。
examples.english: A star is a celestial body that emits its own light.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夜空|よぞら}→夜空：09591_yozora⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧⟦{光|ひかり}→光：01707_hikari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{大部分|だいぶぶん}→大部分：03420_daibubun⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、はるか{遠|とお}く⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧{恒星|こうせい}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ものだ。
examples.english: Most of the light visible in the night sky comes from stars that are extremely far away.

notes:
SIMILAR WORDS:
{恒星|こうせい} (star) vs. ⟦{惑星|わくせい}→惑星：05052_wakusei⟧ (planet): Stars emit their own light; planets orbit stars and reflect light. In everyday Japanese, ⟦{星|ほし}→星：01510_hoshi⟧ covers both stars and planets in casual speech, while {恒星|こうせい} is the precise scientific term.

ETYMOLOGY:
The characters {恒|こう} (constant, permanent) + {星|せい} (star) reflect the historical observation that stars appear fixed in position relative to planets, which visibly move across the sky.
